Pay increases/Bonuses extremely hard to get. 5 years in 1 department with all 2 ratings and 1 pay raise of 3% my last year. All these cons are again totally based on the department you are in. Worked in another department 4 years all 2 ratings highest pay raise 14%  the lowest pay raise 6% which came 5 months after getting an out of cycle 8% merit based increase.

advice:
Reinstate annual cost of living increases and reserve the meritocracy for bonuses. 
Reevaluate the salary scales for sites on the East coast and those within a 60 minute commute to a metropolis.
Allow management to enforce dress code violations or reinstate business casual across all sites.
Set consistent site policies
pros:
Multiple locations around the world, diverse opportunities available
Full benefits, including health, dental and vision insurance, available from start date
Tuition reimbursement available
401k match up to 6%
Telecommuting available for some positions
cons:
Annual pay increases determined by meritocracy and less than 50% of employees are eligible
No annual cost of living increase
Benefit cost to employees increases annually, often resulting in less take home pay year over year
Site policies are not consistent, some allow company sponsored events to take place off site and some do not
Salary ranges for some sites should be increased based on proximity to metropolitan areas and/or region of the United States in which they are located
Dress code policies are not enforced consistently

advice: Management should not survey it's employee for better ways to manage.  If your a manager / leader / officer of the company isn't that your job?  It's frustrating to know big bonuses are being paid to managers who get told how to be better.  If the idea is mine shouldn't i get a cut????
pros: Remote work is awesome for a work life balance.  I work with some very intelligent people.  Lot's of room to grow and learn existing technologies.
cons: As a software developer i want to stay away from making widgets.  I want to work on projects that are interesting, and give me a chance to build new technologies.  Citi as a company isn't focused on this.  They care about reducing cost (as they should), stockholder perception (as they should), etc. I am projecting my career goals here; however, there are limited opportunities to invent.

advice: Listen to your people, give them a chance to provide honest feedback without repercussion, they are the resources that matters.  Forced rankings, inflated VOE scores and the good ol' boy/girl network is driving away the best talent that Citi has.
pros: Still a good place to work with great benefits, vacation time and flex opportunities for your work life balance.  Senior Executive Management has made a big push to improve the employee relationships with management.
cons: The Senior Executive Leaders are engaged, supportive and working hard to improve the Citi image.  This looks and sounds great in the news and in print.  Middle management, i.e. Managing Directors, Directors and the SVP level, they only care about making their bonuses.  They will sacrifice anyone as long as they make their numbers and bonus.  When they no longer have the leverage, either your gone or they take the package and run.

summary: This company is good place for retirement, but not for people who want to make some achievement.
advice: The company should provide more motivation to employees to work  hard to get work done, not reward people for "follow procedures" but never get things done.
pros: Lots of vacation time--I almost feel guilty for having some much time off.  The company is strong and stable. The company provides fitness facilities and nice cafeteria. Some people go to exercises and have a shower during lunch break. Most people go to lunch at company's cafeteria and it is easy to socialize with coworkers. The foods are good and prices are very reasonable.
cons: It is very hard to get things done. Lots of unnecessary and absurd procedures to follow. Some people only care about following company's procedures or policies and keep themselves out of trouble. It is so frustrating if you want to get something done.

advice: The red tape. Really. 3 different systems to raise a database update, and 2 weeks to process this is simply embarrassing.
pros: Salary very high for position. Willing to try new technologies for applications. Management (at least in my experience) has been very nice and approachable. Office is in a very good location of Dublin. Also office is of very high standard.  Overtime is not a major part of their culture in my experience - apart from releases which take part on Saturdays (from home). Ability to work remotely.
cons: All the red tape. My god the issues they have for even requesting the most simple of updates (like database updates for example) even in test environments. In my experience, very little social interaction between employees. Teams can be across different continents (even 3!) which creates time zone issues and lack of clear / constant communication.

summary: Citi has to get out of it's own way
advice: Stock holders, kick out the current board, and re-tool, even dismantle this awkward and unmanageable business.
pros: Citi is a place to learn the craft of banking, within whatever profession one works in, for me, I became both an executive and a talented architect for technology while I was there. It has a smart work force, all dedicated to doing a good job. It has sufficient power in the world, so that a person can build a great external network.
cons: It suffers great paternalistic centralized control, which leads to an arrogance in which the best ideas from below, and from the regions are not given sufficient weight. This leads to frustration in the work force, poor results for the business, and great nepotism in the work place. Most folks I know at citi are simply getting a pay check, hoping things will get better.

advice: Stop listening to the accountants.  People gain experience at the firm and as such are more valuable than anyone who just walks in the door.  To fire the person with experience to replace him with TWO that do not have experience makes no sense.  The two newbies take forever to reinvent and rediscover what the experienced man already knows.
pros: Large firm, secure and intelligent staff ready for support if needed with lots of room for improvement leading to opportunities unparalleled in a smaller better run institution.
cons: Lots of know it alls who really don't know it all.  Too much bureaucracy to be considered a dynamic institution.  They are completely under the government microscope fo compliance and as such cannot move fast even if their corporate life depended on it.  Run by accountants who do not understand the quality of investments in personnel.

pros: Citi is an amazing place., The peer group is excellent and the opportunity to learn is really great! I love working with Citi and would strongly recommend Citi for people who have big ambitious goals in their professional life. Some may consider Citi to have an aggressive culture but it works really for people who are competitive in life. Citi is a large Institution with Highly Skilled & Talented professionals , the workforce is diverse , not just limited to Gender but all walks of life, geography , skill expertise , culture & ethnicity . Teammates are supportive and the management is transparent. Communication standards are very well defined and applied; role and responsibilities very well set. The organization policies are good and offers good benefits and compensations. Overall everyone seems concerned and responsible for what he/she is doing.
cons: Nothing as such, best in everything

summary: Poor Management and opportunity and outright corporate misbehavior
advice: Dump your employee review process. Forcing people into a bell curve doesn't make sense. Managers should be able to make honest reviews of their employees and not be forced into giving undeserved (or unearned) ratings. Listen to people, don't dictate. Figure out who Citigroup is and build it. Don't be everything and fail to accomplish anything.
pros: Good benefits. I hate to say it, but that's about it.
cons: Typically poor management, including severe office politics and under qualified management teams. It would be one thing if people were capable of getting better, but typically management makes the same mistakes over and over. Strategies change very often, with dictates from NY that fail to drive beneficial status, while they refuse to listen to people who know what they are talking about. Management even outright lied in a town hall saying Citigroup had "no significant part in the mortgage security crash" in 2008. Really?

advice: Remember Non-exempt employees matter. A lot of them see all the benefits that exempt employees get and find it unfair when they are working just as hard if not more with no overtime pay. Give them more flexibility.  A lot of them who are are in non exempt roles are not newly graduates, don't get bonuses, and don't get to work from home when this is technically a fin/tech environment. Make them feel valued as well in other ways
pros: There is a start and an end. The team and people that work there are smart/fantastic/passionate. You learn a lot from each other, and the work life balance is great
cons: They do not make non-exempt employees feel valued. If you are exempt you get a lot more flexibility. Even if you get a good year review, you are not guaranteed a merit increase. Salary tends to be on the lower end.

jobTitle: Credit Specialist II Retail Credit Services
pros:
Paid training, and the work is very easy as long as you pay attention; it's just extremely repetitive.

They give great benefits, and almost a months worth of paid time off. You just have to be careful to not go over the "unplanned" time.

There are some good options to move up, but they are free and far between.
cons:
You won't know how to do the work being expected of you once you're done in the training. You'll be put on the floor, and told to read procedures and figure it out, but the people around you are usually willing to help out.

A lot of the problems just come down to bad communication, but management would rather keep saying it's the agents responsibility to stay up to date rather then actually talking with line level reps to make sure everyone understands, and is in a good position to succeed.
jobTitle_clean: credit specialist ii retail credit services

advice: Take ethics complaints more seriously and focus on doing right by people instead of strictly looking at things arbitrarily as dollars and cents. Ultimately if the right thing is done, I do believe that will pay it self back to the company ten fold in so many different ways.
pros: There are a lot of great opportunities throughout Citi considering how large it, and also in the audit department. There is space for promotion or movement in the company between departments.
cons: Because of how large the company and the audit department is, and with teams being compartmentalized, it's also a hit or miss regarding your growth opportunities depending on the team you're on. Some senior managers empower their teams, some don't, and others are outright unethical. But that's to be expected in such a large company, not everyone is going to do the right thing.

summary: Just a big name to work with and tell your friend that I work for CITI
advice: Salary is an important factor  especially on a entry level employees who put in efforts to out stand,work hard and take no leave in their initial period with company. please do give some nice increment package or a nice bonus when contract is reviewed and extended or confirmed.
pros: flexible,good name in banks, work from home, training and vacation benefit
cons: Very poor salary package for beginners, hardly peanuts :(( Infact temporary staff gets 3-4 times the salary then the permanent ones. Very jealousy and unhappy with pay package as it include super and tax which leaves me with nothing. Boss appreciates ur work but no rewards, no bonus, no increment in salary packages nothing.Just very dry Feel like I earn so much but still I don't own anything .Wana go Shopping Spree for ages with a secured bank account ;)

advice: Treat the people that provide your data with respect. Show them that the data is important and it couldn't be done without them.
pros: Health insurance used to be amazing. With the new CEO, things have gone downhill. The culture is great, if you are part of a group. There are fundraisers for the community, pot lucks, and bake sales constantly. The break rooms are full of coffee and vending machines offering anything you can imagine.
cons: They are constantly restructuring the company. They expect people to do the jobs of 3 people. Some of the higher level management is completely clueless. Others are brilliant. You have to hope that you get a good one, or your work life could be awful. There is a lot of favoritism within the company. They promote meritocracy, but employees never see it.

summary: A very 'corporate' workplace with great culture
advice: We invest so many resources to make the workplace great but it would be very beneficial to take one more step and PLAN changes out so that transitions are smooth.  So many things feel pieced together on-the-fly.
pros: We have really great people. Even though there are 1,800+ employees, most people feel like more than a number. Benefits are above average, pay is fair, time off is excellent (146+ hours paid per year), some 4-10hr schedules, lots of overtime opportunities. The list goes on and on. Best environment I've ever worked in; almost unbelieveable for a site this large.
cons: Policies and procedures change frequently and there is always conflicting information (published on intranet, passed down from supervisors, sent around in emails, hear-say on the sales floor, etc.).  The IT infrastructure is lacking: the systems feel as though they were pieced together with no sight of the "big picture."

summary: The worst example of H1B  Culture!  Avoid if you are a non-immigrant.
advice: Hire more Americans.  The current IT staff  that exists is  80-90% H1B immigrant from 6 week technical schools in India and have no idea what they are doing.  This seems odd in a country that is less than .1% Asian immigrant.
pros: There is nothing redeemable about this company from an IT standpoint.
cons:
Everything bad about an H1B 'culture' company.

Like most H1B companies the workforce is underpaid and exploited and the managers (mostly foreign born Indians) are hostile to non-immigrants and operate as if they were running a Mumbai call center.

They will do everything to underpay, overwork, and exploit the working relationship.  When confronted they will lie and/or ignore your emails, phone calls, etc.  This would work well if you were in Mumbai or New Delhi.  However as an American Company they need to do better.

Just do yourself a favor - say no and look for work elsewhere.

summary: Experience in IT very good the first 10 years but over the past 5+ years, morale & environment have gone off a cliff.
pros: Opportunities to advance and learn were great.  Remote work option was encouraged from upper management on down (within IT areas not requiring a physical presence).   Benefits and time off policies are pretty standard for the industry.  Most people work well together (even across disciplines) to get the job done.
cons: Recent management changes placed focus on reigning expenses, with an increased focus on personnel (versus productivity, automation, etc.).  This has contributed to low morale within IT areas.  Company is focused on moving IT staff to lower cost locations (midwest and overseas) and/or outsourcing certain support tiers.  IT management power structure has shifted overseas.  Trust within regional teams has become a major issue between staff and IT upper management .

summary: Citi has a good culture but be aware of layoffs
advice: Stop sending US jobs overseas.
pros: Citi has a good culture in that they care about employees. They took great care during Covid to follow the science and make decisions that kept employees safe. I was able to work from home for over a year and definitely felt that Citi cared about my well-being.
cons: I worked in IT and every year there would be big layoffs. Mostly US jobs in order to outsource to India. This caused a lot of anxiety since I never knew if I would be laid off. Also, this caused time zone issues since we could only have meetings with our Indian counterpoints in the morning. Not an efficient way to manage a project when you're so limited on collaboration time.

advice: Please provide good education on financial planning and products.
pros: I've been with Smith Barney for less than a year now as a Financial Advisor Associate, Smith Barney has a good reputation, technology, and talented employees within the wealth management industry.
cons: The firm only care about how much assets you bring in as a financial advisor. Therefore, the firm train you well on how to prospect relentlessly but you have to basically self-learn about products, how to use technology, and how to do administrative paperworks. You are really independent from day one, and it is quite overwhelming. I was so disappointed by the firm's lack of support in terms of product or financial planning education for new FAAs. You have to bring in about a million dollar a month to be a very successful FA and it is very very difficult unless you have rich family background or established book of business.

advice: At some point, you have to realize that you've cleared out your "dead wood" and that you're now managing out and/or laying off people who are talented and have a lot to offer the company. Rather than assume someone should be let go because they've been there forever, try to see if they can work with new technology or new people.
pros: Great work-life balance. Lots of career-oriented, smart people to work with. Terrific benefits package.
cons: Compensation was far below industry standards and what my peers were making. Promoted twice with any increase in salary. Career mobility options are more limited than they should be for a company of this size, due in part to frequent purges of talent and downsizing. Moving between business areas is almost impossible due to "good ol boy" mentality. Absurdly slow to embrace new technology.

advice: Interesting your stock price and dividends have finally gone up past years, yet you chop employees who have spent decades working hard for you.  You won't keep good talent for long if you keep this up, folks like a certain amount of job security.
pros: Good health and dental benefits, generous PTO policy.  Management pretty hands off and doesn't make you work OT.  Good support for policy questions, co workers friendly and supportive for the most part.
cons: Layoffs are always in play at Citi, so go in knowing at some point your likely to be dispensed. I've seen employees with 10, 20 or more years been chopped over the past several years.  The office environment is pretty lame, but can be better depending on what manager and group you work with.  May or might not get raises every year so don't be shocked if you don't get one.

summary: A great company to complete a career
advice: The only advice that I would note would be to train the Supervisors to be able to perform the same duties as the agents so that they are able to assist more effectively when an agent has some issues with their system or policies and procdures.
pros: Citi Mortgage was a good company to work considering the employee benefits and appreciation.  If employee performance was good, the company would reward the good performance with bonuses.  An employee appreciation activity was held every 6 months. This company always kept employees up to date on training and laws that affected mortgage lending and servicing as well.
cons: The company continually experienced computer issues resulting in excessive amount of down time.  Also, some of the leadership took advantage of their positions and did not assist the employees as needed.

summary: Worked on a business analyst project for the Market Data groups here.
advice: Adjust size of teams for best operating efficiency. Bring in more multi-disciplinary elements to the personnel pools. Technology support here was good: IT was efficient and the right tools were always available for completing the job; if not, they were requisitioned easily.
pros: Smart, friendly, and well-adjusted people. People willing to help whether you're part of their team/project or not. Relatively agile for a large company, good office location and amenities.
cons: Scope of projects I was given were relatively narrow. Typical problems of working in a large organization:  Lots of hoops to jump through to get management or HR/payroll/finance approval for any changes to project parameters or to do simple things like get various approval papers signed for things such as personal trading declarations. The processes for these types of things did go pretty quickly considering the steps involved.

advice: Stop hiring and start investing in the talent you already have - start matching market rate
pros:
If you get the right manager, you will be treated great. Great work/life balance. However if you end up with someone who is new to CITI or hasn't been promoted within 5 years, they will torture your life - give you all their work and make you work towards unrealistic expectations, all while trying to get recognized for themself. 
When interviewing make sure to ask these sort of questions. ..
cons:
2022 update: Bonuses are almost non existent from AVP to VP, expect about 2-3% of base salary. SVP's are around 10-14% . It will take a long time to 'get paid' so take this into consideration when accepting a job .

Promotions above a VP are very rare and take a min of two years in a role to even be considered.

summary: Minimum wage jobs have better working conditions
advice: Upper management needs to open their eyes to what is happing at the middle level IT infrastructure management.THe middle management is overzealous in acquiring and overloading the technical workers.LAyoffs have become very common every quarter even though there is no need.
pros:
Will  get a fancy title
Good 401 K match
Ok benefits to maintain their fortune 500 status
cons: No training at all and you are always at least 3 years behind in the industry.This place has become sliding doors with lot of people leaving the place and management not filling the positions based on cost savings.Oh the positions are out there all the time showing that this place is always hiring.You will know that you are doing the work of five people once you get hired.No bonuses or raises in the past five years.Performance is not valued.Global Talent management is a farce and black and white icon.Wolves all over the place and nepotism to the roost.No value for hard work when it comes to getting rid of people

summary: A very good company for average life expectations, but not the best place for hot-shots and maverics...
advice: plan the actions more carefully, cut back unnecessary expenses & bureaucracy, focus on core business
pros: Good brand name, better compensation then most of the local banks, friendly worker environment, steady workplace if you like, in-house trainings. Also it is easier to find jobs in market after getting labeled as a "previous employee of Citibank". Although the group got smaller, currently it is reorganizing itself, so the change yields to new opportunities to show yourself and go further. If you are interested in a career in banking & finance, Citigroup provides a solid name and opportunities for the ones who wants further in area...
cons: less opportunity to move further, bigger than it should be, senior managements failures in decisions, unnecessary long bureaucracy, rivalry for power between departments (which encumbers the speed of process), unnecessary outsourcing, not enough planning

summary: Too many layers lead to bureaucracy. Lack of accountability. Leading to failed professional performance. Bad medical.
advice: If you need to hire people - then hire more people. People's workloads are already spread extremely thin across multiple endeavors.
pros: I work in Information Security, the leadership is excellent. They listen to their people and try their best to make everything as good as possible. This organization is filled with so many talented and bright individuals. Lots of internal opportunities.
cons: Too many layers, too much bureaucracy. Leading to failed professional performance. No budget for external training. Citi's participation in medical benefits is abysmal compared to other organizations. Compare your current organization's cost to how uch Citi is contributing towards the medical plan. If you have a family, the medical insurance will practically eat 25 to 30% of your paycheck. Yes, they give you so much vacation time - good luck in trying to spend it, the workload is insane here.

advice: Its not 2008 any more.  Plenty of opportunities for employees out there now.  You will continue to lose great talent due to unwillingness to pay for skilled team members
pros: They will pay you just enough to not insult you for your efforts.  They are generous with "thank yous" and other forms of non-monetary encouragement/praise.
cons: You will be out-earned by anyone in a comparable role with a comparable title at any other institution.  If you're hired low, you will stay low, and they will deny you promotions to prevent having to pay you at the right level.  Promotions are given purely on political grounds and being great at what you do counts for very little.  Very senior people with very little skill make elaborate amounts of money and compensation pools are hoarded by these people.

advice: Don’t push our experienced people and replace them in lower cost locations just to save money. Look at what your people contribute to the organization and focus on getting rid of executives who survive via politics instead of looking at the value they add.
pros: Seems like a good place for junior level people to advance to mid level (in technology). Good place to work if you are an officer or associate level looking to make VP.
cons: Very competitive at the senior level. Big push to downsize in “high cost” locations like New York and London.  Poor bonuses while I was there. When I was a consultant (before converting to staff) they actually cut my rate 14% after being there a year after as an executive decision placing a max rate on all consultants in my group. That was demoralizing.

summary: Excellent for customer and pathetic for employees
advice: Very unprofessional of a mufti national company like Citibank to fire people in one day as it affects the career and the family involved with the earning member
pros: money is the only reason to work here
cons: Based on your 3000 calls in a month a single mistake in a single call stops your confirmation. People get thrown out without notice period in a single day, They hire new batch and the very same day ask an old employee to leave and don't even allow the former employee to use the washroom and collect their bag. Very unprofessional. They extend confirmation for 2 months after half year of service and then on the 10th or 11th month without prior notice kicks you out. This practice is very old people don't express this out, as this is a disrespect  and an embarrassment, but few of us found it very insulting and no job satisfaction as the customer's will be bombarding at the phone continuously to us and the supervisors will bombard in your break time, hence we left with dignity.

summary: THE WORSE PLACE EVER TO WORK-- JOB SEEKER BEWARE
advice: Quit making things so complicated. Let your employees structure their own calls- and handle customers with the care any literate person possesses. QUIT changing everything ALL the time.....and for god's sake, quit making your employees feel like they're 3 inches tall because they forgot to place a hyphen in the account notes.
pros: Only thing good about this place is the pay. I can not say any other good words about this place.
cons: HORRIBLE training-- 6 weeks of "learning" absolutely nothing, Managers are just absolutely unprofessional and down right heartless, CONSTANT system issues- which YOU end up getting in trouble over, And the worst part--- Ask one question- and literally get 10 different answers-- and YOU get into trouble, because you didn't choose the correct answer. They expect you to keep up with hundreds of different procedures-- and they change them daily. You don't have time to blink during your work day, and they expect you to keep up with all the changes. This place is just a freakin' joke.....Plain and simple.  Don't waste your time!

advice: Make "The Peter Principle" required reading for all people managers. Foster greater trust and respect of your employees from your management. Curb your hubris!
pros: Competitive pay. Learning opportunities. I had a good starting salary, but few raises over the years, and no bonuses for my last 5 years (even though I was consistently rated an exemplary employee). They paid for me to get a good deal of ITIL training, and once I left Operations, I did have opportunity for growth and expansion.
cons: Politics, Lack of concern for employees. In my 11+ years of constant power-shifts and routine layoffs with Citi, I never felt secure in my job. Through many years of mergers and acquisitions, a culture of fiefdoms developed, which stifled real progress, innovation, and reasonable business management. While pinching pennies on business critical initiatives, they routinely wasted millions on the absurd pet projects of executive "leaders".

summary: A great place to work with! Everyone is represented!
advice: Review employee benefits on medical insurance plan
pros:
Citi PH is a great company. A very established brand in the Philippines. Focuses on diversity and inclusion and has made sure that this is measured by the diversed candidate slate and interviewers. The company also promotes internal mobility. This allows employees to move around, discover new roles within the organization - good way to keep the employees from leaving. 
Has a very nice office location
I would say salary is competitive especially for fresh graduates
cons:
Whilst the bank offers a highly competitive salary, and has shown that it could also adjust to the changing times where focus is on ensuring everyone is well represented, benefits should be reviewed. 
Medical insurance should be extended to parents especially if the employee is single. This would attract more people to join

summary: If your not on phones you may have a better experience
advice: Get better working computer programs so that you can meet the monthly goals and get bonus. Or lower the ridiculous high dollar amounts on the goals. Also allow for phone calls to be complete before you try to ask what went wrong on a call 2 days ago. Translation 300 calls ago.
pros: People and atmosphere was great.  Managers were very knowledgeable about the processes. Also very diverse company.
cons: Collections expectations were too high and systems were not working properly half the time to be able to take a payment much less collect. We were deducted our unplanned time for being late from lunches and breaks even one minute. On top of phones had to adjust your time card or the whole team would be dragged down with percentages. And you were discouraged from getting off the phones to use the bathroom.

advice: Promote growth and take the career aspiration of full time employees seriously. Offshoring looks cheap but in the long run the company ends up paying money for production support due to the code quality and the overal product developed. Good trchnologists won't stay long in such environment. Cut down the bureaucracy setup.
pros: Great work life balance, 401k and healthcare plans. Some good managers who are really good leaders and promote growth, but  category of leaders  is very less as compared to number of managers in Citi.
cons: Offshore and consultant centric environment, promotions and full time conversions  are based on relations, too many SVPs, VPs with no behavioral skills. Less opportunity if you are a tech savvy and a full time employee because all development and design related work is done by offshore.  Working model is not different that any overseas consulting firm with onsite-offshore setup

summary: Great company to work for with lots of growth opportunities!
advice: Less favoritism and more equal opportunities. I myself have not been a victim but have witnessed it with other employees numerous times.
pros:
•Many opportunities to move up within the company.
•Great management 
•Overall positive work environment
•Team environment
•Lots of time off and excellent benefits
cons:
•Can be stressful if on the phones full time, dealing with angry customers.
•Can sometimes feel like a high-school type of environment with favoritism 
•Started out at $12 an hour plus shift differential and received a raise yearly afterwards, however, when the company raised their minimum pay to $15 my pay rate was not raised to match what I should be receiving. Making the same amount as brand new employees is very discouraging after working so hard to be rewarded with raises each year.

advice: The way to fight racism and sexism (real issues) is not to forcefully fill in positions with minorities/women regardless of their actual skills. Build equal chances for them in the workplace instead of simply ignoring white male candidates even if they're obviusly the best. "if you can't find a person of colour for the position i'll send you someone from India" - actual feedback given by a senior manager from India after stating that that due to the social structure in Poland a vast majority of candidates are white males .... the same manager stated during the same conversation that hiring a white male is not an option... THATS REVERSE RACISM AND SEXISM, it's strongarming the problem the other way, not fixing it.
pros: Stability is the only one i see
cons: other then stability pretty much eevrything

summary: Horrible work culture and terrible leadership above the branch level.
advice: Respect your employees and look out for them. Management above the branch level is horrible, but they all look out for each other and blame everything on individual branch production without doing anything productive themselves. Stop scheduling stupid weekly or daily calls to intimidate people and actually do some work to find solutions
pros: Branch level leadership is good in most locations and all of the personal bankers and relationship managers are great to work with
cons: Everything but the listed pros. Terrible culture, intense sales pressure, intense pressure to receive perfect customer service scores which fall disproportionately on the tellers (if a client has a bad overall impression of the company or just had a bad recent experience with the company it will be captured in the teller's customer service survey, despite the fact that they may have nothing to do with it), regional level and national management is a joke; I was dumbfounded by the intelligence level and competence of people who run such a large retail bank

summary: Great place to work and flexible.
advice: I am sure they are doing the best they can, however, I think that leadership roles needs to filled to allow the necessary roles/duties to flow down to the employees and staff.
pros: Working with the team, my team was amazing and I managed my schedule. If I had a doctor's appointment or anything that will take up a chunk of my time during the day, I can make up for it later in the evening. My team did not allow weekend work, so it was nice to be able to work standard hours. However, when we have a project and deadlines, we did anything we could to get it out the door, including working overtime.
cons: Due to the new consent order, there were new teams formed and therefore, the teams were still figuring out their cadence, which there were lots of times spent completing your CPE's and staying up to date with any new compliance regulations and updates.

summary: Management team was abivalent towards new hires and offered no guidance to ensure success
advice: Have a plan for onboarding new employee's -- listen and give creedence to outgoing employee's during the exit interview!
pros: The benefits were outstanding!  22 vacation days, and 12 "personal days" which were to be taken for any given reason...that along with 10 holidays -- astronomical!! They were very concerned with VOE, the Voice of the Employee.  This was a new concept for me as I was surrounded by the mantra "VOC" Voice of the Customer and our bottom line was obviously tied to bringing in new customers and/or clientele.  The Blue Ash facility is outstanding and a real plus to the community.  I think they'll eventually make this facility the de facto Center of Excellence; but it will take time.
cons: The management team in Long Island City was horrendous about assigning responsiblities, guiding new employee's or offering constructive feedback.  I knew that I had made a mistake after just 3 weeks of accepting a job with them.

advice: More effort needs to be done to retain junior people. If not, the analyst group will continue to be a revolving door. And once the senior employees retire, there will be no experienced bodies to fill those roles.
pros: The best thing there for me was the quality of the people around me. With that said, upper management often was disconnected.  The 401k 6% match with immediate vesting was also very good. Depending on which group you're in, work life balance can be good as well.
cons: Commercial banking is in decline with relocations and outsourcing being performed. Wages also aren't going up. Even with a promotion, you won't get paid more. This isn't a Citibank problem exclusively though, the banking industry is changing. Lots of senior people continue to work there just so that they can hold on to their pension, otherwise, they would've jumped ship already.  There is no longer a pension for junior analysts, so with no retention incentives, there is high turnover.

advice: Stand by your word that when your employees are effected by a job being discontinued, that those employees get a "first look" at job opportunities. Myself and many others have applied to get back only to either get no response or not even a interview to come back.
pros: Some of the best benefits in the area as in vacation and sick time and 401K. Really enjoyed most of the people I worked with. A great number of employees were very dedicated to the company.
cons: Below ave pay, but some benefits made up for a little. Many of the promotions were based on who you know. It appears lately that they have been getting rid of tenured people only to cut costs. Many tenured effected by outsourcing of their jobs are not being hired back for other positions like promised. Citi used to celebrate their long term employees, however now dedicated employees are treated poorly and have no sense of job security like it once was.

summary: "Bad Salaries & No good benefits in Chile"
advice: Open your eyes, give bonuses to people, don't retain the money, use that money for retain good talents...better salaries...people are not agree with Chile Citi policies, when i came to citi i thought that a big company, an international company, gives better salaries and bonuses... very disappointed, i see smaller companies, with better benefits .
pros:
Working as a team, not competitive at least in our group.
Working from home.
cons:
Under market pay
No career grow opportunities.
No Bonuses.... train people please, not CIti Courses that have no certifications!!
Have to work hard with excess of Hours are not paid, Fridays late working with no life(almost every release).
Don't retain good talent.
Compensation is not always aligned with performance.
HR, that has to help employees, only helps their interests, horrible team.
They ask you to stay late, but when you need to leave early they dont let you.

advice:
Less politics Citi  
Learn to treat people respectfully - people literally yelled at me through the phone  "You don't know who I am ? I am ---- I have been with Citi over 20 years".
pros: Citi is large and has robust process. You will learn everything you need to know about oiling the machine. You will get to work with interns to Managing Directors.  You will get to work globally and have lots of work and learn.
cons: The company has such a high workload per person that nice people are rude because they are crushed by the volume of work. It is very corporate still and manual. There are times you need to copy the same information up to 3 times. Because of the size approving anything takes time and many people need to be involved

pros:
the team was great, very helpful, always ready to answer any questions. Our manager was very approachable with any concern regarding performance and overall feedback; supervisor teams the same way. 
Great atmosphere, great over-time pay. 
Good advancement opportunities.
cons:
Vacations needed planned in almost a year ahead. 
Any last minute emergency was not really appreciated as the call volume would increase and team performance would drop.
Culture was very lazy, people with absolutely no life goals surround you in every department and majority of co-workers felt to me as they were scared of expressing their true opinion about certain management issues and overall new rules. 
Paid maternity leave was horrible, especially if you are already pregnant when you join (had 2 girls in my team, different stages in pregnancy and each pay was worst than the other)

summary: Rewarding experience but need to be flexible to adapted to senior management turnover.
advice: Citi needs to catch its breath and change from brute force cost cutting to more strategic investments in redesigning old processes and technologies as a means to gain sustainable efficiencies.
pros: Fortune 100 company with a very large global footprint.  A great number of the best and brightest individuals. Strong and stable balance sheet.  Significant financial and human capital to invest in innovative solutions.
cons: The culture tends to be passive/defense where interaction with people is guarded so that  individuals are more concerned with their own sense of job security - don't rock the boat.   The tumultuous nature of the banking industry itself reinforces this culture. Starting with the sub-prime mortgage crisis of 2008, restructuring, outsourcing and workforce reductions are common in the big banks.   At Citigroup, senior management turnover has more frequent than other banks since the 1998 Citicorp and Travelers merger.

advice: Continue to look  within your ranks to address new gaps in leadership positions. It promotes ownership. Senior technology purchasing decision makers do not listen well to their senior technology staff and have frequently increased the cost to do business by choosing a less viable solution that looked cheaper on the surface.
pros: The men and women at this company work very long hours to do a good job at what they do. They have many experienced management and technical staff to help the businesses make money as efficiently and highly performing as possible.
cons: There are so many good people working here its difficult to accomplish a single task that does not impact several other tasks and goals.  If you cannot be patient and navigate the various interests involved it can be frustrating but may not lead to promotion in any case.

advice: Reward effort with money and not empty skype messages. We don't need weekly emails about masked diversity at CITI when basic principles are dishonored everyday. Train your managers and team leaders. Introduce mentorship for entry level jobs. Do something.
pros: Work from home. Medicover. Flexible.
cons: Low starting salary. Yearly pay raise around 2-4% which is extremely disappointing. Close to zero chance of getting promoted in your own position. Non-existing reward system. Everyone I know is severely unmotivated and looking for another job as an escape. Disorganization at every level. Applications that used on daily basis are horribly optimized and often unavailable, hence the work delay. Incompetent backup system. Even if you put an actual effort in your job it doesn't matter, so eventually you will not put any effort in your job. People also leave because of the heavy workload resulting much more heavy workload because of their absence, BUT there is no hiring to replace them. Surveys are completely ignored even if they are really bad (and they are really bad). You will stuck doing the same thing for years if you don't push yourself really hard.

advice: Shake up the culture, the reason the business hates the IT is because the IT executive leadership doesn't care about anything that doesn't immediately boost their resume (head count and budget).
pros: Large stable company with hefty compensation packages.  The idea of working on very large scale systems supporting mission critical financial services can be a nice challenge.
cons: Executive team had little care of real issues and focused strictly on cost per head count regardless of any other factor.  The technical teams in Dallas and St Louis had resigned to a life of not caring anymore.  The company lacked any kind of energy, with most employees readily telling you they are there to collect a check.  We saw critical system fixes delayed 9 months because no one wanted to actually do the deployment.

summary: If given an opportuntity to work at Citi again I would be more than happy to do so.
advice: Keep staff up to day with current events. Motivate them, appreciate them, respect them, reward them and allow them to be able to approach you to discuss any matter they may have. Happy staff ensures productivity & complete satisfaction
pros: Throughout the years I worked with an amazing group of people. Acquired knowledge and understanding of the commodities clearing process.  It was a daily challenge to learn new processes which were also beneficial in my day to day job functions.
cons: In extreme cases of data processing and heavy trading it could have been long days ensuring the job gets done. However there were always unexpected and unpredicted issues which caused management to seek resolutions to avoid next day problems.

advice:
Manage the office politics and vet folks before promoting to mid-level or managerial roles. Will be nice to have qualified next in line candidates participate in EQ and Management training before being promoted. 

Invest in remote work to expand/retain top level performers
pros:
1. Plethora of opportunities (put in the work and be rewarded especially if manager relationship is great!)
2. Continuous learning and development opportunities 
3. 1.5 to 5 percent yearly salary raises
4. Diverse to some extent 
5. Competitive benefits
cons:
1. Work life balance especially with a demanding manager
2. Some mid-level managers not qualified for their role
3. Lack of communication from mid-level to bottom
4. Pay rate below the average salary
5. Relies heavily on offshore and that can at times impede work quality or output 
6. Limitation in career advancement if not in the right group

summary: mixed bag because of crappy mid-level managers
advice: please look closely at why so many awesome resources are leaving in the Cyber Security space.. got to the root cause
pros: you get to work with some very smart folks in the cyber security space (infra pentesting, redteaming, cloud, devsecops, application pentesting etc.) One gets to be part of an awesome global firm with a great brand recognition as well work with cutting edge technology
cons: mid level management sucks.. they have been entrenched for ever and do a crappy job. new CISO and his team are awesome but they do not really know what is happening 2 -3 levels below them. several awesome resources left in the last 2 years because of crappy mid-level management ( MD, Director level and SVP level) and not because of better pay etc..

pros: Salary is a little better but that is it.
cons:

2. It has a very bad crowd. People, they talk all the time, they don't even care that they are disturbing other people. 

3.  You don't have a preassigned desk, you have to find an empty desk. You also have to clear your desk after work.

4. Every desk has a VDI and you are supposed to connect to your remote machine with the help of VDI. Everything is very slow, and the machine hangs all the time. Even you cannot connect your headphones to the VDIs.

5. A lot of people do support work and get over 300 emails every day (not exaggerating), bad place to learn anything technical, just remember it is a bank. 

6.  You are expected to work over 10 hours every day.

7. They don't have coffee machines, unlike most companies. 

8. Dirty restrooms,  you will feel as if you are in a public restroom.

summary: lack of corp wide UNITY. The focus should be many, many groups, but only ONE COMPANY.
advice:
cut in half upper managment.  

focus --> everyone works for the same company.  

Hire American.
pros: looks good on your resume.
cons:
lack of corp wide unity.   All the purchased companies that make up this giant,  will not work as one.... 
there are parts of company directly competing with other parts of the same company... or taking food from 1 hand and putting in other hand...the net results is minus zero, if you consider both groups, man hours spent.
many seniors thinking they that are above the law, for short term gains, but should think for longer term. off shoring may help bottom line for next several quarters, but will hurt 3 to 7,  years out.  It takes 2 or 3 Indans to replace 1 American

summary: Had High Hopes, Shattered by Citi Management
advice: Global Markets shoud sack all IT directors and managers in Columbus and start over with a completely new slate.  They are not willing to change in order to pull Citi back up.
pros: I was asked to return to a company Citi recently acquired in 2007.  With that, I believed that the job that I was doing was going to help our clients and our staff be successful.  Instead the dysfunctional organization continued to spend money on bad decisions and upper management was not held accountable.  I delivered my work on-time, bridged fractured client relationships and began making end-roads to baselining our staff with Citi's delivery model.  Suddenly, I was caught in the middle of the 50,000 person layoff and yet am the only senior project manager who was relieved of their duties.
cons: Day-to-day, staff are not sure what changes are going to happen.  The management staff in Columbus don't talk with clients, their own staff which leads to no one really knowing where the intiatives are going.

summary: Escalated concerns of customers is being handled by one person in the Manila site; Information systems too complicated
advice: Management of Citibank BPO Philippines(outsourced by Australia) should assign more workforce (experienced employees) to be delegated more tasks to resolve customer escalated concerns of Citibank's Australia's bank customers--not only assigned to one officer (who cannot be contacted but through email-not to mention the long response time). If this is implemented, the campaign for lowering the site's average handling time would be facilitated
pros: The Information technology being used are up to date; Salary is fair and reasonable for employees with experience
cons: Information System Software are not user-friendly--too complicated; Escalated concerns are being handled by one person (female) in the Manila Site (in other places officers cannot be contacted also) and cannot be contacted by anyone for follow-ups--main reason why Australian Customers who have escalated concerns are not happy with Citibank Australia Customer service

summary: Working for Citi is as good as you can stand it.
advice: Pay yourselves less.
pros: The benefits package has been very very good throughout the years, although it has also gotten more and more expensive.  It pays well but expects 150% for that payment.  Do not start there thinking it will be a breeze, it is not.  No one has been treated well, and they are all more than willing to share the misery.  But like I said it pays better than most places in this town.
cons: Long hours, expectations from management that are unclear, senior management seems unclear on anything.  Rewards are few, and are given to the people who promote themselves the most, or the people whos management takes the time to recognize them.

advice: All management should be required to have at least a bachlors degree.
pros: Good Benefits. They offer multiple schedules. Not a bad choice but not something you'd want to stay at for as long as I did, hind site 20/20 I wish I would have went back to school and learned something more valuable, they make it so easy to stay on the hampster wheel with all the vacation they offer and you do have job security or at least I did.
cons: Pay to retain employess is horrible to say the least and Management is some what to be desired. If your just looking for a "job" this might work for you. Its one of those kinda jobs where you need to drink lots of koolaid, you are the hampster on the wheel.

pros: There are a lot of training opportunities
cons:
Citi says it supports a work-life balance and lets employees work remotely.  Then it uses the fact that work can be done successfully while remote to justify moving the job to cheaper locations.
The matrix relationships between managers is crazy -- its pretty hard to figure out who works for who & what the real priorities are when you report to three different people at a time.
It's just too big -- it shouldn't be as hard as it is to get things done, but the organization is so complex that even the little things take forever to accomplish.
Its still very much an old boys network and doesn't take the time to really groom managers.  Some of the behaviors they reward are really beyond belief.

advice: Screen applicants better. Make sure they don't just want a job (or a transfer to New York). Consider moving downtown.
pros: Brand recognition. Since the building is relatively new, it has many amenities, such as a large cafeteria and a gym. Good place to start if you are a college grad.
cons: Lots of people came here because either they had no choice, or want a transfer to New York. People tend to leave after only a few years, which causes significant knowledge loss (not to mention that procedures are rarely written down). This and combined with low pay, contribute to the negative vibe you will may feel. Also, due to the site reaching capacity, parking can be terrible if you come in late, or need to run an errand during the day.

summary: Citigroup & Wall Street - Is it all the same?
advice: Hire strong leadership at the middle levels, there is little talent their and all are focused on self preservation and large bonus checks, not about building strong teams and growing employees.  Lower level managers are completely unempowered to grow and incentivize their people.
pros: Flex hours, work from home when needed.
cons: Benefits get worse every year, it's a race to zero.  No growth, no bonus regardless of performance.  Bell curve evaluation process, somebody must get a poor review even if everyone performs well.  New hires are over compensated with lofty titles and bonus guarantees, while existing loyal performers get no growth and no bonus.  Toxic work environment, when the going gets rough, the fingers start pointing.  Lot's of in-fighting and empire building.

summary: Relaxed environment where you can achieve as much or as little as you'd like
pros: Great Benefits - 401k does a 6% match which from what I've seen is unheard of for this type of large non-tech company. Use an online 401k calculator and you'll see it basically guarantees you're a multi millionaire by retirement if you start straight out of college
cons: Depends on what you want our of your career. If you want to dedicate your life to your job and potentially come out with many millions of dollars, then this is probably not the right place to do that. BUT, if you would like to live a well balanced life and guarantee a strong financial future then this is definitely the perfect company for that.

summary: You will be challenged, and hopefully rewarded.
advice: Act on the voice of the employee feedback provided by the entire employee population; reward outstanding workers, else risk losing them.
pros: You will be challenged and given opportunities to show your leadership. Professional advancement opportunities are available, but you have to seek them. If you're lucky enough to have a seasoned manager, he/she will show guide you through the Citigroup jungle, and help empower your career. Flexible work-life balance, if you schedule and communicate well with your management is possible.
cons: Excessive regulatory and audit scrutiny drain resources from more productive projects. You have to take charge of your schedule early on, else you will be a blackberry (aka crackberry) slave. Some evidence of old school, micromanagers still exist, although senior management is working hard to change that culture.

summary: Very disappointed, that after years of dedicated service I was cast aside for a few dollars in savings.
advice: Upper Management should treat it's employees like human beings and not cattle. You lose a lot of credibility when you thank long time employees for their hard work and dedication one week, and the next that their job is being moved offshore to save money. It really shows that dedication only flows in one direction at Citi.
pros: Good Pay, Excellent benefits, Many hard working dedicated employees.
cons: Very Long hours put in will go unappreciated. Upper management will give you lip service, but as I found out, it really means nothing. They Claim to care about their employees, especially long term ones, but at the end of the day all they really care about is the bottom line.

summary: Lack of leadership and interest in creating a unified culture that motivates the workers.
advice: Retire and let better blood take the wheel before the company goes down like the Titanic
pros: I can say with openness that the only good thing about Citi or Citigroup right now would be the fact that you get a pay check, as small as it is; oh yea insurance.  Other then that you will have a J-O-B with minimal pay
cons:
The board of directors have lost vision and direction, and are unwilling to make the "real" decision required to "right the ship".  The executive group "click" are not truly interested in fixing any of the real issues, instead they are only interested in ensuring they get their bonus, which they have NOT earned.

If I were in charge I would remove the cancer from the executive team, clear the deck all the CxO's at corporate and sector levels as well as their 1st, 2nd and 3rd Lieutenants.

advice: Office politics have are taken to an extreme at Citi.  In an organization so large, groups are constantly fighting over resources and hording information.  There is no sense of teamwork among the groups.  With moral sinking based on the massive layoffs the protectionism is only getting worse.
pros: Citigroup hires really bright people with big ideas and drive.  The compensation package is excellent.
cons: There is no work life balance at Citi.  My colleague had to cancel a trip to Italy for a project and he had already paid for the tickets.  The other issue at Citi is politics.  Turf wars are  common practice and institutional knowledge is something that is guarded and shared only when absolutely necessary.

advice: you are building a house with a foundation of sand as long as you refuse to treat your core work force with respect and consideration.
pros: Great benefits, some real talent in middle management.
cons: uppper management completely misses the concept of noblesse oblige, and since they seem to think of themselves as nobility, this is a problem. They make arbitrary changes mid stream, leak the info to every company under the sun, but fail to inform their employees what is going on. Employees are shuffled around into positions they never applied for and would never have accepted if given any input into their own lives. Upper management feels that the people who do the bulk ofhte in the trenches work areirrelevant,  expendable, and replaceable in that order.

summary: Good people, hard work and no work/life balance
advice: Management should start to value their employees by giving them comp days or salary revues.  They are going to burn out at the rate that they are working.  Eventually something will give and either it will be quality of the work or employees leaving the firm.
pros: Because of the size of the firm, there is always room for advancement and growth.  There are a lot of very sharp people and almost all of your peers and teammates are pulling together for a common goal.
cons: They pay you as little as they can get away with.  Work/life balance is non existent.  Be prepared to work long days, frequently into the night and on weekends with no additional comp.

advice:
Good place to work overall.  Id work there again.

Comment on VOE:  Great that you do them, they are a real plus.  Note that if an area has a low VOE score, there is a solid reason why and you need to replace the person getting the score.  It takes several years to "escape" from a bad manager/senior manager and as people leave, the scores may look like they are improving temporarily.

 If very senior managers aren't actively doing their own exit interviews (at least a phone call), they don't really know what's going on.
pros: Good people.  Good work.  Good company.
cons: Middle management may have poor leadership skills.  Despite "Voice of the Employee" attempt to get upper management feedback on their middle managers.

advice: Practice good ethics in dealings with liens and employees.
pros: Hard to get fired and you don't have to produce.
cons: Unethical practices perpetrated against the client and employee, even if a borrower can bring their account current within the month citi's management requires you to place them on a deferment so they can get the $1000.00 from the tax payers, the Irving Texas location had 250 work outs in January 2013 which netted them $250,000.00 for the month , just from federal handouts, and their stated goal is to double that amount over the next two months.  I came to this department promised many thing and out and out lied to. I just purchased a home a few months ago, I got my loan from Wells Fargo.

summary: Great place to work, but depends on the project
advice:
E-mail oriented development is not a good design process for software.
We had a horrible manager in my last months at the company who badmouthed who was not around. It was sickening and mass complaining to the HR did not seem to have any effect. The team's mood was horrible and people were lacking motivation because of that. It was a bad move to not act on this in a timely manner.
pros: I work in IT where almost everyone was friendly and brilliant. Many interesting projects and advanced technologies is use, and lots to learn. Great work life balance.
cons:
Internal processes are inefficient. Even a 4 year old PC upgrade required months of waiting.
Thousands of e-mails exchanged every day, it was overwhelmingly bad.

advice: Choose better people to promote. Don't use experience as the main factor, use talent.
pros: Citi has good benefits and competitive salaries. I did not think that the work was that demanding or challenging, which may be a pro or con, depending on what you are looking for. There is definitely room for career growth and plenty of opportunities globally.
cons: Citi's management is mostly incompetent. They make poor decisions and fail to listen to their employees. Also there were a lot of lay offs/restructurings while I was there. Mostly people in NY were being laid off and jobs were moving to low cost areas. Training/onboarding new employees was another weakness of Citi's. Also the bureaucracy inhibits efficient work from being accomplished and prevents innovative changes from being implemented.

advice: Adopt the peer review system where the performance of employees can be more transparent and give more frequent promotion opportunities based on the performances. Also, avoid giving too much power to the HRs who are trying to hire the employees for cheap; rather, give more power to the employees and managers who can chase after the best employees and give what they deserve
pros: Excellent 401K plan (6% match), good medical and life plans, very flexible schedule (WFH), supportive management teams, tons of training and volunteer opportunities
cons: Lack of a bonus since the economic downturn in 2009 crash, somewhat inefficient promotion opportunities, bad team culture due to hiring many under-qualified contractors and employees than the best talented employees, only partially competitive pay salary

summary: Lack of integration makes Citi a difficult place to find success.
advice: Citi needs to do a better job of integrating the various business segments.  There is a tremendous amount of talent not being utilized to its full capacity which is preventing the organization from performing as a global leader.
pros: As a large organization with a tremendous amount of locations and resources, opportunities to work in other states in various departments are available.  The organization also values work/life balance and encourages time off along with providing flexible working conditions.
cons: Due to frequent restructuring at the senior management level, the strategy is continuously changing.  Coupled with the various silos created from all the M&A, the lack of cross-communication can make it extremely difficult to share best practices and network with internal talent.

summary: Good place to work for those who thrive in an ever changing environment
advice: Be more decisive; even in the dynamic industry you are in.  Perhaps under Jane's leadership this will happen.  Would save a fortune in throw-away work.
pros: There are some wonderful, dedicated people at Citi to work with. If you appreciate working in an environment where there is a LOT of change, this could be the place for you.  There isn't time for complacency, which I found highly appealing. This also gives you an opportunity for a great deal of learning.
cons: Sometimes you feel as though you are spinning your wheels due to the constant change.  Some folks are not cut out to work in this environment; if not...this isn't the place for you.

summary: Lot of work pressure, unreasonable deadlines, No work life balance
advice:
Start thinking about employees. 
Keep realistic goals.
Be civilized
pros:
You get to see every sort of technology.
You work with lot of smart, energetic, dedicated but aggressive people
Work from home option only for certain teams. 
Good vacation package, good benefits.
cons:
You should spend lots of overtime at work. Management would not help in any way. Work is expected to be done all by yourself as an individual. No team work. Management is involved(sort of directly provokes) directly in conflicts within colleagues. 
Lots and lots of politics. You cannot survive with out developing very thick skin to tolerate. 
No salary raises. If there are, they are very low compared to the long hours you spend. 
Very bad work culture.

advice: More opportunities for personal growth in part-time positions is absolutely necessary. As a collector that routinely does full DCF analysis and values companies at school, I'd really appreciate the opportunity to offer more value to the company.
pros: I work part time, 20 hours a week, really relaxed environment, management will bend over backwards to accommodate my school schedule. They have been fantastic to me over the years, excellent benefits through Manulife, unbeatable for part-time work and flexibility.
cons: Monotonous job, negatively toned conversations with clients, its like you start on the wrong foot with every conversation, takes a lot of patience and the ability to be able to handle these clients and turn them into a positive conversation and relationship.

advice: Recognize and reward your quality people.
pros: A lot depends upon your manager.  Assuming one has a good manager, one can almost define his/her role by taking on as much responsibility as possible.  If one has the aptitude and drive getting exposure to technology, quants, analytics, trading desks, etc. are all within reach.  Internal mobility is supported and encouraged.
cons:
Because this is a very large organization, there is a need to cooperate with many peripheral groups and coordinate schedules and project plans.  There are formal meetings and processes to accomplish this, but it also helps to have a good network of friends when you need favors.

Even top performers are seeing compensation compression in these difficult economic times.

Also maybe alternate days when employees have to be on the phone & working Queue apps. More Schedule options to where like day options where they could work through the week and alternate a day no the weekend every other just more options would be great....

cons:

Having to wait so many years to have a shift changed which is hard on family time.

advice: Try to look at peoples work ethics, qualities and desires. Not just who they are or how they interview.
pros: Benefits and job security are good. Tuition assistance, and time off make working here a little more acceptable. Possibility to grow with the company if you know the right people.
cons: Working in a call center makes for long days that are always the same. Customer are rude because they don't have to look you in the face. If you are ok working with ungrateful customers regardless of the situation this is the job for you. Schedules usually are not great and it is a lot like being somewhere between a high school and a grade school. Job is easy and repetitive.

advice: Stop allowing employees to coast for years on end, update employee reviews to a modern system that’s about them and not company goals, offer real prescription drug coverage instead of prescription insurance through CVS Caremark which forces employees onto generic drugs delivered through the mail with no customer service help. Invest in US workers instead of hiring foreign nationals. US workers are the minority in my location.

With all the efforts to increase employees' mental health (upgraded facilities, ping pong & foosball tables, etc), it would go a long way towards actually improving that by using some of those funds to staff appropriately and provide necessary headcounts so employees don't get burnt out.

advice: Get out of the limousine, away from the sycophantic handlers, and mingle with frontline and operational employees to see the challenges they're facing, and then actually commit to making things better instead of just returning to "business as usual". pros: A resonably competent, intelligent person will have an easy time at Citi. But you will have to deal with a lot of stupid people, especially in the "management" bureaucracy. And you would do well to remember not to care, no matter how much they try to force you to care, because otherwise you'll be very unhappy caring about stuff that doesn't matter.
cons:
Management constantly tries to overtake your life, applying ridiculous pressure to achieve goals that were assigned by people who have no clue, on timelines that bear no relation to reality. Always push back because there's no punishment; they just want to intimidate you into getting more work out of you for less money. If you accrue overtime, they'll often make you roll it over into another week where you'll work fewer hours, so they don't have to pay overtime rates. Citi is already involved in a class-action lawsuit over that practice, but they keep doing it.
Citi laughably reveres the uninvolved upper management as "the seniors". Title inflation is rampant. A simple team lead/supervisor is labeled Vice President, President or Director.
Employees have good benefits but no work-life balance. Having 5 weeks of paid vacation is useless because you can never take it when you want, only when management says you can. Usually they just tell you to take a week off, with no warning, so you can't plan for anything. Then they still expect you to work on your vacation.
Citi harps on "compliance" and following all sorts of rules, but they often follow only the letter of the rule-- there is a well-established workaround for every rule.
Citi relies heavily on Indian and Pakistani contractors, so women at Citi often suffer from a hostile work environment. If you're Indian/Pakistani, black, lesbian, transgender, or ideally a combination of all of those, you're in a "protected class" at Citi. Everyone else, not so much.
Remember, banking is one of the worst industries to be in (like farming, only with less death and dismemberment). Pay is low, morale is low, opportunity for advancement is low. So in that regard, Citi is typical. There are MUCH better places to work. I work here because it's convenient and I don't have to work hard for the money. But I would not recommend Citi to anyone as a career, or as anything more than a stepping stone to your next job at a different company. "Soul-sucking stupidity" is a good summary of the work environment at Citi.

pros:
* If you can get in here at the beginning of your career, then you will learn a lot as they have some of the best product, marketing, and operational processes along with financial discipline that I have experienced in my career to date.
* As things happen at light-speed at Citi, sideward promotions are done quickly so you can move around the different teams within a business unit quite quickly. Upward promotions are another story (see cons).
cons:
* Unlike other organisations, Citi is extremely tight with expenses. Everything is analysed to death before a decision (normally a "no") is made. I noticed a big pull back around the GFC, and it didn't let up many years thereafter. I believe this stifles innovation and risk taking, and unfortunately I see that Citi has gone from an innovator to a follower.
* Middle management is too focused on protecting their own nests and fighting for the top promotions when they come up from time-to-time.
* The overall culture in the bank is dog-eat-dog -- people are generally so overworked and competitive that they aren't willing nor have the time to help you...and why would they help a competitor for a future promotion that they're going after?!
* The pay is really average compared to the big 2/4 - like I said, really great place to learn but terrible if you want to get financially recognised for your experience.
* Overall, there seems to be a lack of cohesiveness with the strategy of the consumer bank -- do we just focus on the Credit Cards business which is a cash cow, or should we actually become a proper bank and accept deposits and write mortgages? The branch network is orientated towards Asian investors, and sends a mixed message.

Outsourcing the the already outsourced, when will it end?  Outsourced workers in India are rude, demanding, and when you can understand their broken and incorrect English, are terrible at what they do. advice:
Quality of work should almost always be the primary focus for a company.

I had a coworker who was tasked with maybe two projects and when he couldn't do anything else he literally slept at his desk. Management was blind to it for years. He's actually fairly skilled and reliable but he slept or twiddled his thumbs because management just wanted him to occupy a seat for 8 hours a day. Ridiculous! Of course if I was him I'd seek out work when I'm caught up with my projects, but it can be tough because management never had a steady stream of projects. But they sure as heck wanted you to warm a seat in the meantime. How that makes any sense is beyond me. I understand being available for when people need you, but it's called being on call. 

Also there were times I had to remote in to my computer when out of state. Remoting requires updated Java, which is impossible to do on most public computers (library, hotels, etc) without an administrator password. On top of that most browsers are changing their defaults to disable Java and/or ActiveX. In other words, make sure you bring a laptop and test connecting ahead of time before considering working while away.

Also please consider updating your websites and applications to support newer browsers. Windows 10 is shipping with Edge now and I believe they no longer ship with even IE 11 installed. Which means any sites and apps which require them (most that I'm aware of) will not function in the future.

Consider using server blades to run virtual desktops for even your on site staff to cut down costs and make it easier to maintain. I swear half my coworkers are trading out parts on a quarterly basis.

Also thin apps may cut down on licensing costs. It will also allow even cheap laptops to run expensive processes off more than powerful enough servers.

Quit screen scraping! What a ridiculous process. Very error prone and inefficient. Start working with teams to pull data from files and datasets that are on mainframes. On that note, start giving your transactions IDs so when you submit washes and credits you can link it to the corresponding debit.

Seriously consider the benefits of switching to multithreaded applications and normalizing databases. There are so many inefficient processes and database designs that could be exponentially improved by a programmer who knows what they are doing.

Good base salary, but plan on leaving after a couple of years of not getting a reasonable raise and/or bonus.  Typical raise OR bonus (you will not get both) is 0-2%.  Oh, if you are somehow rated top performing, you will get 4-5%.  
If you work for the wrong organization/management, you will have a bad experience.

advice:
To fire the folks who’s work culture doesnt fit citi’s standard.

Have multiple L1 round to decide on L2 and hire folks who are right fit for the team adhering to citi principals
pros:
